{{2015–16 Big East men's basketball standings}}
The '''2015–16 Villanova Wildcats men's basketball team''' represented [[Villanova University]] in the [[2015–16 NCAA Division I men's basketball season]]. Led by the school's 8th head coach [[Jay Wright (basketball)|Jay Wright]] in his 15th year, the Wildcats were members of the [[Big East Conference]] and played most of their home games at [[Finneran Pavilion|The Pavilion]], with some select home games at the [[Wells Fargo Center (Philadelphia)|Wells Fargo Center]]. The Wildcats finished the season with a record of 35–5, 16–2 to win the [[2015–16 Big East Conference men's basketball season|Big East regular season]]. They lost in the championship of the [[2016 Big East men's basketball tournament|Big East tournament]] to [[2015–16 Seton Hall Pirates men's basketball team|Seton Hall]]. The Wildcats earned an at-large bid to the [[2016 NCAA Division I men's basketball tournament|NCAA tournament]] as a No. 2 seed. In the Tournament, they defeated [[2015–16 UNC Asheville Bulldogs men's basketball team|UNC Asheville]], [[2015–16 Iowa Hawkeyes men's basketball team|Iowa]], [[2015–16 Miami Hurricanes men's basketball team|Miami]], and overall #1 seed [[2015–16 Kansas Jayhawks men's basketball team|Kansas]] to earn a trip to the Final Four, the fifth in school history (although the [[1971 NCAA Division I men's basketball tournament|1971 Final Four]] season was vacated by the NCAA). In the Final Four, the Wildcats routed No. 2 seed [[2015–16 Oklahoma Sooners men's basketball team|Oklahoma]] by the largest margin in Final Four history to face No. 1 seeded [[2015–16 North Carolina Tar Heels men's basketball team|North Carolina]] for the national championship. Led by [[NCAA basketball tournament Most Outstanding Player|Final Four MOP]], [[Ryan Arcidiacono]], the Wildcats won the [[2016 NCAA Men's Division I Basketball Championship Game|National Championship]] 77–74 on a three-point shot by [[Kris Jenkins (basketball)|Kris Jenkins]], assisted by Arcidiacano, as time expired. The Wildcats won the school's second national title, having previously won the [[1985 NCAA Division I men's basketball tournament|1985 NCAA tournament]].

Their 35 wins were the most in school history, breaking a record of 33 wins set the [[2014–15 Villanova Wildcats men's basketball team|previous season]]. In beating No. 3 seed Miami (AP No. 10), No. 1 seed Kansas (AP No. 1), No. 2 seed Oklahoma (AP No. 7) and No. 1 seed UNC (AP No. 3), Villanova became the first school in 31 years — since the [[1984–85 Villanova Wildcats men's basketball team|1985 Villanova Wildcats]] — to not only beat four top-three seeds on the way to a national title but to also beat four straight opponents ranked in the AP top 10, in addition to beating AP ranked Iowa in the Round of 32, by an average victory margin of 19 points per game. Villanova's run included two of the ten most offensively efficient games in the analytics era (2002–present), beating Miami and Oklahoma by scoring 1.56 and 1.51 points per possession in the Sweet Sixteen and Final Four, respectively.<ref>{{cite web|last1=Gasaway|first1=John|title=Best Offensive Performances|url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/story/_/id/15460067/10-best-offensive-performances-10-years|website=ESPN|date=May 5, 2016 }}</ref> It has been called perhaps the most dominant tournament championship run of all time, and the most dominant of the analytics era by a wide margin.<ref>{{cite web|last1=Winn|first1=Luke|title=The Five Most Dominant Tournament Runs of the Analyics Era|url=https://www.si.com/college-basketball/2016/04/14/villanova-wildcats-national-championship-title-game|website=SI.com|date=April 14, 2016 }}</ref>

10 years after Villanova's championship run, three key members of the team in [[Mikal Bridges]], [[Jalen Brunson]] and [[Josh Hart]] led the [[New York Knicks]] to their first [[2026 NBA Finals|NBA Finals]] win in 53 years, with the trio starting every playoff game and Brunson being named Finals MVP.

==Previous season==
The [[2014–15 Villanova Wildcats men's basketball team|Wildcats]] finished the [[2014–15 NCAA Division I men's basketball season|2014–15 season]] 33–3, 16–2 in [[2014–15 Big East Conference men's basketball season|Big East play]] to win the Big East regular season championship. They defeated [[2014–15 Marquette Golden Eagles men's basketball team|Marquette]], [[2014–15 Providence Friars men's basketball team|Providence]], and [[2014–15 Xavier Musketeers men's basketball team|Xavier]] to become champions of the [[2015 Big East men's basketball tournament|Big East tournament]]. They received the conference's automatic bid to the [[2015 NCAA Division I men's basketball tournament|NCAA tournament]] as a No.1 seed where they defeated [[2014–15 Lafayette Leopards men's basketball team|Lafayette]] in the Second Round before losing in the Third Round to [[2014–15 NC State Wolfpack men's basketball team|NC State]].

With their 31st win of the season, a 63–61 win over [[2014–15 Providence Friars men's basketball team|Providence]] in the semifinals of the Big East tournament, the Wildcats set a single season record for wins, which would eventually finish at 33.
